coc: For a cocontinuous functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ between sites, denote by $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})$ the associated morphism of topoi, with direct image $g_*=({}_su)$, where $({}_su)$ is the sheaf-valued right Kan extension, and inverse image $g^{-1}\mathcal{G}=(u^p\mathcal{G})^\#$, where $u^p$ means precomposition with $u$. When $u$ is also continuous, its inverse image preserves all limits and admits the left adjoint $g_!\mathcal{F}=(u_p\mathcal{F})^\#$.
adj: Let $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ be cocontinuous with a right adjoint $v:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}$. Let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})$ be the associated morphism of topoi, with $g_*=({}_su)$ and $g^{-1}=(u^p-)^\#$. For a presheaf $\mathcal{H}$ on $\mathcal{D}$, write $v_p\mathcal{H}$ for the left Kan extension of $\mathcal{H}$ along $v$ as defined using the opposite of the category of arrows $V\to v(X)$.
loc: For a site $\mathcal{C}$ and an object $U$, let $\mathcal{C}/U$ be the category of arrows $X\to U$, made a site using those families whose underlying arrows form coverings in $\mathcal{C}$. The forgetful functor $j_U:\mathcal{C}/U\to\mathcal{C}$ is continuous and cocontinuous, induces a morphism of topoi $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$, and gives the adjoints $j_{U!}\dashv j_U^{-1}\dashv j_{U*}$. The functor $j_{U!}$ is extension by the empty set and $j_U^{-1}$ is restriction.
